title: Some Aspects of a Metallurgist’s Electron Microscopy Toolbox in Memory of Jim Bentley
content: Dr. Jim Bentley and the author of this presentation were graduate students together in the research group of Prof. Michael Loretto at the University of Birmingham (UK). We both later immigrated to the US with Jim joining a National Laboratory and myself a university. We have both shared the excitement of using electron microscopy in our daily research careers, having developed a very keen interest in characterizing microstructure. In this talk, as examples of research performed over the years, three topics of electron microscopy will be described, being defect analysis, structure determination using convergent beam electron diffraction, and determination of site occupancy in ordered compounds. The first of these has been well described in [1], and the second in publications such as in [2] and [3]. Site occupancy is a difficult task, and in this talk at first the Ordering Tie-Line construction will be described [4]. Then, the possibility to make use of aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopes with x-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy (XEDS) with detectors having large collection angles to perform spatially-resolved measurements will be discussed. Importantly, the possibility (or probability!) of phonon scattering causing electron scattering from the incident beam direction onto adjacent atom columns will be discussed [5].
